title: Why Reiki Doesn’t Work | Scientific Truth
description:
Reiki is marketed as a mystical form of energy healing, but in reality it is nothing more than pseudoscience. Practitioners claim to channel a universal “life force” through their hands to heal everything from fatigue to cancer. Yet science shows no evidence of such energy fields, and every well-designed clinical trial concludes that Reiki is no better than placebo.

Invented in the early 20th century by Mikao Usui after fasting and hallucinations, Reiki has spread worldwide thanks to clever marketing. From “attunement” rituals to promises of distant healing, it thrives on faith, not facts. In India and the West, Reiki healers promise cures for serious illnesses while offering nothing more than suggestion and conditioning. This is dangerous when patients delay proven medical treatment for empty hand-waving rituals.

A comprehensive review by Edzard Ernst and randomized controlled trials at institutions like the Scripps Institute found zero measurable energy and no therapeutic effect. The supposed warmth, tingling, and relief that people report are classic placebo responses. Reiki survives because of testimonials, scientific-sounding jargon, and people’s desire to believe, not because of evidence.

Reiki belongs in the same category as homeopathy, Ayurveda, and faith healing — pseudosciences that violate basic laws of physics and chemistry. Claims of channeling invisible life forces cannot be falsified and offer no credible mechanism. Worse, Reiki training has no licensing standards; anyone can become a “master” with a quick attunement ceremony.

If you’ve searched for Reiki explained, Reiki debunked, Reiki placebo, Reiki scam, Reiki pseudoscience, or alternative medicine hoaxes, this video lays out the scientific perspective.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video so more people can see through pseudoscience and demand evidence-based healthcare.
